Hæc iterum formula mox a Rege ad Parlamentum rursus mittitur tabulario inferenda, præcipitur omnibus Regni Præsulibus, & Ecclesiasticis ejusdem subscriptio, dictatur pœna jacturæ, seu confiscatio bonorum, amissionis beneficiorum, quin deportationis &c. Obtemperavit pars longe maxima Episcoporum, minasque pœnarum canonicarum addidit. Harduinus Perefixus eodem anno ad Archiepiscopatum Parisinum evectus inter primos mandatum subscriptionis per dioecesim suam vulgat, & anno sequente 1665. Portum Regium tam Parisinum, quam Campensem lustrat, Virgines ferocius renitentes una cum Agnete a S. Paulo Arnaldi forore, & Parthenonis Antistite ejicit, variisque monasteriis includit, cæteras, Sacramentis interdicit.

Quo doloris sensu factio nidum suum tam subito disturbatum viderit, facile est divinare. Trepidatio primum ingens, tum clamores: hinc tormenta, & lugubres threni persecutionem veritatis, & innocentiæ deplorantium; hinc diræ, quidquid sacræ profanæque dignitatis erat, devoventium: tumultuatum denique inter ipsas factionis partes, atque per plures annos præsentis sæculi usque decertatum. Cum enim passim tam vigili Episcopo-

rum constantia, quam fevera Regis jussione ad subscriptionem urgerentur, plurimorum rigida Moralis haud exiguam labem passa est; subscripserunt, quin errorem animo deponerent, pejerarunt, ut sua sibi retinere, aut ad nova aspirare liceret. Qui tenerioris erant, aut videri volebant conscientiæ, circumspiciebant subterfugia, & media, quibus horrorem mitigarent perjurii, & ad æquivocationes, atque restrictiones mentales confugiebant, quas vel laxissima Moralis horreat. Sie primam damnabant propositionem, dicebantque, justis omnibus dari gratiam, qua ipsis mandata Dei possibilia fiant, si eam a Deo, ut oportet, petant: sed animo retinebant, gratiam orandi, ut oportet, non omnibus justis dari. Secundam damnabant, quia gratiæ parvæ Jansenii, quæ desiderium boni debile tantum in nobis excitat, inferior simul est delectatione terrestri, (intellige) cui vincendæ sufficiens non est, utique resisti potest: quia, apud se addunt, semper resistitur. In tertia damnarunt, & rejecerunt ex animo necessitatem (puta) naturalem, seu physicam, quæ non per electionem, sed per impulsum facit agere. Circa quartam & quintam juxta scriptum trium columnarum discurrebant, dicebantque, sine dubio prævenie…

Harduin de Péréfixe, elevated to the Archbishopric of Paris in the same year, was among the first to publish the mandate of subscription throughout his diocese, and in the following year, 1665, he inspects Port-Royal both in Paris and in the countryside, and casts out the Virgins who were resisting more ferociously, together with Agnes of St. Paul, the sister of Arnauld and Abbess of the convent, and shuts them in various monasteries, and interdicts the others from the Sacraments.

It is easy to divine with what sense of pain the faction saw its nest disturbed so suddenly. First, there was huge trepidation, then cries: on one side the torments and mournful laments of those deploring the persecution of truth and innocence; on the other side, curses of those condemning whatever there was of sacred and profane dignity: finally, there was tumult among the very parts of the faction, and it was contested for many years of the present century. For since they were being urged everywhere to subscription by the constant vigilance of the Bishops

———— page break ————

and by the severe command of the King, the rigid Morality of many suffered no small stain; they subscribed, without laying aside the error in their mind, they perjured themselves, so that they might be allowed to retain their own for themselves, or aspire to new things. Those who were, or wished to seem, of a more tender conscience, looked around for subterfuges and means by which they might mitigate the horror of perjury, and took refuge in equivocations and mental restrictions, which even the most lax Morality might shudder at. Thus they condemned the first proposition, and said that grace is given to all the just, by which the commands of God become possible for them, if they ask it from God, as they ought: but in their mind they held that the grace to pray, as they ought, is not given to all the just. They condemned the second, because the small grace of Jansenius, which excites in us a desire for good that is only weak, is at the same time inferior to earthly delight, (understand) to the overcoming of which it is not sufficient, it can certainly be resisted: because, they add among themselves, it is always resisted. 47. So ihr einen sehet / so saget ihr / er sey der Teuffel / und hänget ihme lästerische Namen an / und schreibet / man soll von Stadt und Land bannen. Herr Primarius / weiset mir in euren bannen / doch euer Christlich Herz.

48. Seyd ihr Christi Hirt / wo ist euer Liebe / damit uns Christus hat geliebet? Damit wir einander sollen auch lieben / heisset euch die Schrift austreiben / und ins Elend jagen / ohne Verhör der Sache? Was saget sie euch / so du siehest / daß dein Bruder ein Heyd ist / so gehe zu ihm / und straffe ihn in geheim / folget er dir / so hast du ihn gewonnen / wo nicht / so nimm noch einen Mann zu dir / und straffe ihn in geheim / folget er dir / so hast du ihn gewonnen / wo nicht / so zeige ihn der Gemeine an / höret er die Gemeine nicht / so halte ihn für einen Heyden / nicht außjagen / unerhöre lästern und verdamen / wie ihr mir habt gethan.

Parisiis.* Nihil in ea deletum, nihil correctum; Bossueti solum annotationes operi instar clypei præfixæ.

Obstupuerunt boni omnes, donec Sanctandreasnus Bossueti Vicarius, qui omnia, quæ ab Episcopo hoc in negotio acta sunt, testis & arbiter noverat, turpissimas fraudes detexit. Tum enimvero indignatio omnium erupit, delatum opus ad sacra tribunalia, antidota contra pestem quæsita. Interea Quesnellus post Arnaldum caput factionis constitutus, & Gerberonius sparsis per Belgium, & Gallias seditiosis, ut supra relatum fuit, libellis capta præsertim occasione ex memorato casu conscientiæ, miscebant omnia; jamque effrænis istorum hominum licentia nonnisi injecta vi compescenda videbatur. Sed hic labor erat. Quesnellus mutatis frequenter latibulis, ac vestibus, fictisque nominibus, modo P. Prior, aut Provincialis Augustinianorum, modo Dominus de Frefne, Frekerberg, Baro de Rebeck, du Puis &c. dictus industriam sagacissimorum hactenus eluserat.

Gerberonium Bruxellis extremo urbis angulo extractum cepit. Quesnellus deinde ipse cum individuo suo socio Brigodeo, qui licet romanis literis monitus, ut urbe discederet, mutato tantum contubernio in domum *Refuge de Forest* dictam se receperat, ibidem deprehensus, ope socii manus imminentium satellitum jam evaserat, sed memoria cartarum, quas oculis hominum subducere maximi momenti erat, revocatus a latentibus custodiis mense Majo interceptus, feria 4. post Pentecosten in Palatium Præsulis pariter perductus fuit.

Tribus haud amplius mensibus ibi Quesnellus hæsit. Contribules enim, cum omnes obirent rimas, quo aditu opem ferrent, schedula tandem plumbo e fenestris detracto ad Ernestum Canonicum S. Gudulæ inscripta de loco, situ, & conditione custodiæ suæ moniti, murum labore per binas noctes continuato perforant, & ita 13. Sept. …

…with Moral Reflections upon each verse. Paris.* Nothing in it was deleted, nothing corrected; only Bossuet's annotations were prefixed to the work like a shield.

All good men were stunned, until Saint-André, Bossuet's Vicar, who as witness and arbiter knew everything that had been done by the Bishop in this affair, exposed the most shameful frauds. Then indeed the indignation of all erupted, the work was referred to the sacred tribunals, and antidotes were sought against the plague. Meanwhile, Quesnel, having been established as the head of the faction after Arnauld, and Gerberon, having scattered seditious pamphlets through Belgium and France, as was related above, having taken the opportunity especially from the aforementioned case of conscience, threw everything into confusion; and now the unbridled license of these men seemed as if it could only be curbed by the application of force. But this was the labor. Quesnel, frequently changing his hiding places and clothing, and using fictitious names, now called P. Prior, or Provincial of the Augustinians, now Monsieur de Fresne, Frekerberg, Baron de Rebeck, du Puis, etc., had until then eluded the industry of the most sagacious men.

———— page break ————

But at last, the Archbishop of Mechlin, Humbert William de Precipiano, after he had subjected to canonical penalties in the year 1700 another priest of the Oratory, Van Hame, who was spreading lower principles of faith despite repeated warnings, and in the year 1702 instituted an action against Quesnel in Rome, having been provided in the following year with surer clues of his hiding places, first captured Gerberon in 1703, extracted from the extreme corner of the city of Brussels. Quesnel then himself, with his inseparable companion Brigodeus—who, although warned by Roman letters to depart the city, had merely moved his lodging to the house called *Refuge de Forest*—was discovered there; by the help of his associate, he had already evaded the hands of the imminent bailiffs, but being recalled by the memory of papers which it was of the greatest importance to keep from the eyes of men, he was intercepted by the hidden guards in the month of May, on the Wednesday after Pentecost, and led likewise into the Palace of the Prelate.

### JURAMENTUM ELECTI.

EGo NN. in Decanum hujus Capituli canonicè electus spondeo, voveo, & juro, Deo Omnipotenti, Beatissimæ Mariæ Virgini, sanctis Apostolis Petro & Paulo Patronis ejusdem, me Jura, Privilegia, consuetudines antedicti Capituli pro viribus contra quoscunque defensurum & observaturum Confratribúsque modo præsentibus & futuris consilio & auxiliô subventurum, contra neminem ipsorum querelam à quocunque suscepturum, nisi sub duobus aut tribus juxta Apostolum testibus omni exceptione majoribus. Dolo & fraude seclusis. Sic me Deus adjuvet, & hæc sancta Dei Evangelia.

I, NN., canonically elected as Dean of this Chapter, pledge, vow, and swear to God Almighty, to the most blessed Virgin Mary, and to the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, the patrons of the same, that I will, to the best of my ability, defend and observe the Rights, Privileges, and customs of the aforementioned Chapter against all people, and that I will assist my Confreres, both present and future, with counsel and aid. …es, non sine lessu tamen ob mortem Quesnelli capitis sui post Arnaldum æstimattissimi, a quo omnis hæc causa præsens ducta est. Non hic viri hujus vitæ historiam texere lubet, duo tantum iis, quæ jam de eo dicta sunt, memoratu digna juvat addere. Primum est scriptum quoddam ab ipso Quesnello Sacerdoti cuidam missum, qui abstersa tandem errorum caligine, sibi, & Ecclesiæ redditus illud prodidit. Regulæ erant 12. articulis comprehensæ, quibus sui in conversatione inter se & cum vario hominum genere uterentur. Summa ferme hæc erat: Unio, & concordia: arcani fides: circumspectio in sermone pro varia hominum conditione: amphibologia in variis capitibus Religionis: uti Christum in Eucharistia præsentem, neque tantum per fidem, aut figuram, ut heterodoxi, sed neque per transubstantiationem, aut substantialiter, sive realiter, ut Catholici ajunt, dici volebat: quomodo igitur? modo imperceptibili. In Sacramento pænitentiæ attritionis insufficientiam, & necessitatem contritionis perfectæ urgerent. Gratiam sufficientem, libertatem indifferentiæ, merita modo aperte impugnarent, modo per verborum ambages, ut pressis exitus pateat: Gratiam victricem unice extollant: & sic alia plura. Alterum est

At ex quo furor hominem abripuit, anno 1719. Amstelodami extrema senectute ad mortis confinia deductus, quarto ante obitum die rogatis duobus testibus appellationem suam innovat, sicque accepto a Pastore suo viatico vixit 2. Decembris annorum 85. senecio.

…add two things to what has already been said about him that are worth noting. The first is a certain writing sent by Quesnel himself to a certain priest, who, having finally wiped away the mist of errors and being returned to himself and to the Church, produced it. They were rules comprised in 12 articles, which his followers were to use in conversation among themselves and with various kinds of men. The sum of it was almost this: Union and concord; fidelity to the secret; circumspection in speech according to the various conditions of men; ambiguity in various chapters of Religion; he wanted it to be said that Christ is present in the Eucharist, not only by faith or figure, as the heterodox say, but neither by transubstantiation, nor substantially or really, as the Catholics say: how then? in an imperceptible way. In the Sacrament of Penance, they would urge the insufficiency of attrition and the necessity of perfect contrition. They would openly attack sufficient grace, the liberty of indifference, and merits, sometimes directly and sometimes through the maze of words, so that an exit might be open for the pressured: let them exalt only victorious grace: and so many other things.

The second is a notable testimony of truth given by the man himself. Quesnel, asked by his nephew Pinfon, a sculptor, to which party of those then litigating about matters of Religion he should adhere, responded by letter: "He should hold himself to the greater part of the faithful, or firmly adhere to the trunk of the tree of the Church; for he himself had not been provoked and compelled to foster these disputes so pertinaciously except by the injuries of the Jesuits." Pinfon asserted that he had heard the same from Quesnel's own mouth not only once, with the Bishop of Angers, Poncet de la Rivière, as witness in his *Reflexions consolatoires* .
